textile.title: Tami/ Kenetami. Wooden spindle with bende (weight) and yole (dish). Brown string and unworked cotton wrapped around object. Shell pivot missing. Made by a woman.
Misi. Wooden loom with sample of palm fibre weaving attached.
A hammock made from twisted fibres strung between two wooden struts. Rolled into a bundle.
Sadgi. Sleeping mat made of palm fibre ('fasi or fosi). Rectangular, woven, tan or natural colour; some loss to surface due to broken fibre.

household.title: Корзина. Сусу. Гвинейская республика, конец ХХ в.

Hoe. Curved iron blade (.1) with rounded end and long tang, now detached from the wooden haft (.2). Haft is cylindrical in cross-section with a bulbous end through which is set the square socket. Socket end stained darker than rest of handle.
Reaping hook. Curved iron blade, sharpened on the interior curve. Cylindrical wooden handle, split at the end.
Adze. Curved iron blade in straight wooden handle.

Rat trap. Object consists of a woven cone, attached upon a wooden base, with a broad square and narrow rectangular openings on opposing sides. Also affixed to the base at two points is a curved wooden stick, held at tension by a fibre string adjacent to the square opening.
Ke fudi. Plain wooden spoon comprising of an oval bowl and right-angled handle. Small hole present in bowl of spoon.
Lefai. A fan made of woven kenkai or fair palm. Rounded shape that comes to a point at one end, and a short handle at the other end.

Baude ba kefwi. Large wooden spoon with flat bowl and straight handle. One side of bowl and both sides of handle feature burnt decoration, consisting of zig-zags, crosses, and arcs. Some of the decoration on handle has possibly been painted with black pigment. Used for putting rice in a pot.
Wulunyi. Wooden mortar; cone shaped with circular base.
Large wooden spoon with flat bowl and straight handle. Burnt and incised decoration present on one side of bowl and both sides of handle; consists of curved and geometric patterns.
Kanikadebe. A plaited basket of natural colour with a round open mouth, and rounded sides that transition to a square, flat base.

Fish trap, likely cylindrical in shape, constructed of openwork plant fibre and curved wooden strut supports. Trap accessible through both ends through a partially obscured circular opening. Very damaged.
Sule. A stake and strand fish basket made of fosi, or palm mid-rib, with a wide mouth, rounded bottom and a square base with four points. Rim has started to become unwoven.
Circular wooden bowl with flattened base. Semicircular piece missing from rim.

garment.title: Рубаха западносуданского покроя. Сусу. Гвинейская республика, середина XX в.

Shackles or leg irons. Two horse-shoe shaped strips of iron with loops at either end and an iron bar through these loops. The iron bar has a loop at one end with an open spiral ring through it, and a 'T' at the other end. The metal is a little rusted and there is some white residue.
Pair of wooden sandals. Z 14459.1 has a braided fibre strap tied with cloth attached. Z 14459.2 has a hide strap attached, and a long crack present in the wooden base. Worn by men.

ceramic.title: Long, cylindrical bowl, or possibly gong, with rectangular hollow. At one end is a biconical projection, at the other a flattened 'paddle' like projection.
Fenye. Ceramic ink pot, used by Muslims. Ink made of wungili (tu).

arms.title: Simple bow with split cane string. Wooden bow with D-shaped cross-section, notched at both ends; split cane string tied to both ends. Splits along the length of the bow.

Knife with an undecorated wooden handle with a roughly circular cross-section. Blade is undecorated metal, flat on one side with a curved cutting edge. Set into the wooden handle, with a collar of metal.
Hooked knife for rubber with an undecorated wooden handle and a thin hooked blade. Small hole bored through the end of the handle, which has been threaded with a piece of fibre cord.
Susu. Axe head made from pecked and ground stone with a slightly curving blade. Thick patina present on the surface of the stone.
Wobe. Cane stirrer comprising of a long straight shaft and two side protrusions at the top, resembling an arrow shape. Made from a single piece of cane.
Wobe. Cane stirrer comprising of a long straight shaft and two side protrusions at the top, resembling an arrow shape. Made from a single piece of cane.
Two arrows with iron heads. Long, twisted iron point with single barb at the tip, attached to a straight cane shaft with a length of cotton cord. Likely used with bow Z 14445.1.

jewelry.title: Tuniniyi. Long necklace made from roughly shaped beads made from tree root and tightly strung on fibre. The beads are variable in their shape and size, but all have a small hole drilled through the centre.
Borikwori. Necklet or string of small black beads made from seeds. The ends are not joined, but appear to be broken.  Each seed has a hole drilled through the centre.

Piece of bark used as a cure for dysentery.
Deke. Beehive with a cylindrical stake and strand woven body, tapering slightly at both ends. Either end of the hive is sealed by disks formed from spiralled cane. Slightly damaged.
Net. Tightly coiled dyed fibre of a dark red and orange hue. Stored in a bundle.
Belaxana sui. Two small rings with raised ridge around the circumference. They are carved from palm kernel and have a dark exterior, one with lighter natural spots.
Kale (tu). Reed pen with pointed edges, used by Muslims.
